# Results — Study 637 (FOMC Vol Crush)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the VIX
collapses the afternoon of a scheduled Fed decision**: the statement lands mid-afternoon ET
(2:15 pm, 2:00 pm since 2013), the ^VIX close prints at 4:15 pm, so scheduled monetary
uncertainty should resolve into the decision-day close, on a calendar you can set your watch
to. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every
number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is
dropped). Fingerprints `e876dcb8d22b` (^VIX) / `d0ce62443ce7` (SPY) / `a876bb11537c` (SVXY).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily ^VIX OHLC (8,178 rows) + SPY raw OHLC (8,177 rows), 1994-01-03 → 2026-06-30; SVXY adjusted closes (3,705 rows), 2011-10-04 → 2026-06-30 |
| FOMC calendar | **hardcoded** table of **261 scheduled decision dates** 1994-02-04 → 2026-06-17 (Federal Reserve historical FOMC calendars; scheduled meetings only, no inter-meeting/emergency actions — same table as sibling studies 67/135/322/517) |
| Events | all **261** decision days sit on the ^VIX tape, vs **7,916** other trading days |
| Statistics | Welch *t* for the group splits (non-overlapping single-day events); **Newey-West (5 lags)** *t* on the decision-day dummy regression as the serial-correlation-robust cross-check; Wilson interval on the hit rate; 20-seed × 1,000-draw random-calendar placebo |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention (third axis only): SVXY entered at the **prior session's close** — the calendar is public years ahead, zero look-ahead — and exited at the decision-day close; one round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV; long-only, no borrow |
| Data quirks (named) | the scheduled 2020-03-18 meeting was pre-empted by the 2020-03-15 emergency action; the scheduled date stays in the table (it was the pre-announced decision date *ex ante*). ^VIX is an index — its 4:15 pm ET close postdates the 2:00/2:15 pm statement on every decision day |

No survivorship on the Signal axis: ^VIX and SPY are indices, not survivor panels. **Named on
the third axis:** SVXY is the *surviving* retail short-vol ETP — its twin XIV was terminated
after 2018-02-05 ("Volmageddon"), so any short-vol ETP backtest rides the vehicle that lived.

## The headline — decision-day ΔVIX vs all other days

| quantity | decision days | all other days |
|---|--:|--:|
| mean ΔVIX (points, close − prev close) | **−0.415** | +0.014 |
| mean Δlog VIX | **−1.97%** | +0.07% |
| gap | **−0.429 pts** | |
| Welch *t* (points / log) | **−3.51 / −3.94** | |
| Newey-West *t* (dummy regression, 5 lags) | **−3.47** | |
| hit rate (VIX down) | **172/261 = 65.9%** (Wilson 95% [60.0%, 71.4%]) | |

The crush is **real and mechanical-looking**: the average scheduled decision day knocks
~0.4 vol points (~2%) off the VIX by the close, against a flat unconditional day, and the
split clears the desk bar three ways (Welch, log-Welch, HAC). **Random-calendar placebo:**
observed −0.415 pts vs placebo mean +0.016 (sd 0.105) over **20,000 draws (20 seeds ×
1,000)** → **p = 0.00005** — essentially no random calendar of 261 days produces it.

## Event window — run-up and persistence (ΔVIX points, Welch *t* vs far-from-meeting days)

| offset | −5 | −4 | −3 | −2 | −1 | **0** | +1 | +2 | +3 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| mean pts | −0.050 | −0.079 | −0.014 | **+0.301** | +0.050 | **−0.415** | +0.020 | −0.105 | +0.120 |
| Welch *t* | −0.53 | −0.79 | −0.18 | **+2.27** | +0.35 | **−3.45** | +0.10 | −1.22 | +0.82 |

- **Pre-meeting run-up:** cumulative [−5..−1] is **+0.209 pts/meeting** at one-sample
  *t* = **+0.90** — a mild, *uncertifiable* build-up. The only individually notable pre-day is
  −2 (+0.301, *t* = +2.27); the "VIX ramps into the Fed" folklore is at best faint.
- **Persistence:** day +1 is **+0.020 pts** (*t* = +0.10) — the crush does **not** bounce
  back. It is a level reset (uncertainty genuinely resolved), not a one-day dip that mean-
  reverts.

## Realized SPY range on the same days — implied collapses while realized is LOUD

| metric | decision days | other days | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY (H−L)/prev close | **1.557%** | 1.296% | **+4.04** |

The decision day is a **noisier-than-average** day for the S&P itself — yet implied vol still
collapses into its close. That is the cleanest signature of *uncertainty resolution* (the
event premium priced into options expires with the event), not of a calm afternoon.

## Era contrast — pre vs post the press-conference era (split 2011-04-27, justified: first post-meeting press conference)

| era | FOMC-day ΔVIX | n | within-era Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1994 → 2011-04 | **−0.549 pts** | 139 | **−4.81** |
| 2011-04 → 2026 | −0.262 pts | 122 | −1.21 |
| Welch *t* of the difference (late − early) | | | **+1.15** |

The point estimate has roughly halved in the press-conference era, but the difference is
**not certified** (*t* = +1.15) — and the recent slice alone (*t* = −1.21) cannot certify the
crush by itself. The honest reading: the full-tape effect is decisive; the modern-era
magnitude is smaller and noisier (more of the resolution now happens in VIX *futures* term
structure ahead of the day, and 2020-03-18 sits in this slice).

## Third axis — can retail capture it with SVXY held for the decision day only?

Enter the prior close (calendar public years ahead — zero look-ahead), exit the decision-day
close; 118 scheduled decisions since SVXY's 2011-10 inception.

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| gross per event | **+58.9 bps** |
| net per event (5 / 10 bps one-way) | **+48.9 / +38.9 bps** (~ +3.9% / +3.1%/yr at 8 events) |
| all-other-days SVXY mean | +10.9 bps |
| Welch *t* (FOMC vs other days) | **+1.58** |
| hit rate | 61.9% |
| worst single decision day | **−10.5%** |
| post-deleverage era (−0.5×, since 2018-02-28) | gross **+14.7 bps/event**, Welch *t* = **+0.24** (n = 67) |

The point estimate is positive and survives costs on paper — but it **fails the certification
bar** (*t* = 1.58 < 2), and the honest decomposition is worse: since SVXY halved its exposure
after Volmageddon, the per-event edge is **+14.7 bps at *t* = 0.24** — statistically nothing.
One bad decision day (−10.5%) erases two years of net edge, SVXY tracks VIX **futures** (which
pre-price much of the crush into the roll ahead of the meeting), and the vehicle class itself
carries gap-to-zero risk (XIV, 2018-02-05). The crush lives in the untradable spot index; the
retail echo is thin, uncertifiable and tail-heavy.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic mean-reverting vol index with scheduled pseudo-decision days every 32nd business
day and a TUNABLE planted crush; no network.

| world | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (crush = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.04** (sd 1.04), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted crush = 1.0 pt (seed 637) | **−15.67** |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up on a planted crush. *(A faithful-engine /
power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** Decision-day ΔVIX **−0.415 pts (−1.97%)** vs +0.014 on all other days:
  Welch *t* = **−3.51** (points) / **−3.94** (log), Newey-West *t* = **−3.47**, hit rate
  **65.9%** (Wilson [60.0%, 71.4%]), random-calendar placebo **p = 0.00005**, and the crush
  *sticks* (day +1 ≈ 0). Clears **t ≥ 2** on the real tape several ways. Caveat, said out
  loud: the post-2011 slice alone is −1.21 — smaller and noisier lately, though the decay
  itself is not certified (*t* = +1.15).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** You cannot buy the ^VIX index. The retail expression (SVXY, one
  decision day) shows +48.9 bps/event net *in sample* but at Welch *t* = **1.58** — and
  **+14.7 bps at *t* = 0.24** since the 2018 deleverage — with a −10.5% worst day and a
  vehicle class that has already gapped to zero once (XIV). The tradable echo is
  uncertifiable; the beta/costs/tail eat the rest.
- **"Retail can bank it with a 1-day SVXY hold"? — MIXED.** Paid on average in sample (62%
  hit, +49 bps net/event), but statistically uncertifiable at *t* = 1.58, roughly zero since
  SVXY halved its exposure, and one bad afternoon eats a year of edge. The folklore is not
  *wrong* about the direction — it is wrong that the edge is bankable.
